quests.title: Know the Keep
quests.description:
Commander Vane. Before we go any further - can you find the latrines?

I'm not joking and I'm not testing your sense of humour. I don't give orders to people who can't find the latrines, because an order is a place and a time, and somebody who doesn't know this keep will give me neither.

So walk it. Three stops.

The lower court, inside the gate. The middle terrace. And the graveyard wing, west.

That's the whole of the Sepulcher and it takes twenty minutes, and every soldier I've ever had refuse this has cost me more than twenty minutes later.

Then come back and tell me what you saw.

And don't touch anything that isn't yours.

The graveyard wing in particular. Half of what's lying about out there was laid down on purpose by somebody who's still at this keep.
quests.accept_text: The lower court, the middle terrace, and the Raven Hill graveyard west.
quests.turn_in_text:
You didn't fall off anything.

That's a better start than most. I've lost two down the terrace steps and neither of them was being careless.

quests.title: The Woods Below
quests.description:
Now something simple, and I'd like it kept simple.

This keep sits above the pines. That's the whole of its value - everything that comes up this hill has to come up one road, and I can see all of it.

The pines are full of worg, and the leavings of the plague.

I'm not asking you to clear the forest. I want to be plain about that because people get ambitious about forests and forests do not care.

I want the approach to the gate kept short of anything with teeth.

Short. Meaning: a courier coming up that road at dusk should be able to see the gate before something decides about him.

That's the actual measure and it's how I've run this post for two years.

The woods south of here, along the road you walked in on.

Worgs and ghouls both. I don't rank them - they're equally bad at the same distance.
quests.accept_text: The woods south of the Keep, along the road up.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fewer teeth on the approach.

I'll note it in the ledger, which is where things go to be true.

quests.title: A Dispatch for the Rear Guard
quests.description:
A dispatch, for Captain Vesk at the Rear Guard.

It is three lines long.

I want you to know that before you carry it, because people assume a sealed dispatch is substantial and then feel cheated, and a man who feels cheated talks.

Three lines. That's all the situation warrants and Vesk would resent more.

I'd like it delivered by somebody who won't read it.

And failing that - and I've been at this long enough to know which way that generally goes - by somebody who won't remember it.

Those are different requests and the second one is the one I actually rely on.

North along the road. Vesk is at the gate.

He's always at the gate. In two years I have never once had word from him that wasn't sent from a gate.

objectives.label: Deliver Vane's dispatch to Captain Vesk at the Rear Guard

quests.accept_text: North along the road to the Rear Guard. Vesk is at the gate.
quests.turn_in_text: Three lines. Of course. It's rude, and exactly right.

on_accept.name: Vane's Dispatch
on_accept.description: A single sheet, folded thrice and sealed with the Keep's black wax.

quests.title: Shards of the Faithful
quests.description:
Relic Hunter Darne. Don't crowd the table.

I pay for grave-goods. That's the trade, it's legal enough for this valley, and I'd rather you heard my version than Molsen's.

The skeletal groundskeepers at Raven Hill carry the best of it.

Ring-shards, buckle-bone, whatever a person was buried with - and the groundskeepers have it because they've been picking it up for years, out of the plots, and putting it in their pockets.

They're not robbing anybody. That's the part I'd want said. They're tidying, in the only way that's left to them, and they've been tidying since before the Keep had a garrison.

So what I'm doing is taking it off something that tidied it off somebody else.

I've made my peace with that. You'll make yours or you won't.

South, at Raven Hill. Intact - and don't chip them. A chipped shard is worth a quarter and tells you nothing about who it belonged to.
quests.accept_text: Off the skeletal groundskeepers at Raven Hill, south.
quests.turn_in_text:
These are good. Old and honest.

The collectors in the Undercity will weep, and then they will haggle, and then they will weep again.

quests.title: Marrow Work
quests.description:
Yseult. Sit, don't sit, it's all the same to me - but mind the shavings, they get into everything.

I carve bone. Combs, buttons, and occasionally regret, which sells better than you'd think in this valley.

The risen husks out in the field have the best marrow.

I've worked with every bone a person can get hold of here and I'll stand behind that. Fresh is too wet. Old grave-bone crumbles at the second cut. The husks are dry all the way through and they hold an edge where you put it.

And they never complain about the harvest.

[She does not say that like a joke.]

Wherever the field is thickest.

Dry marrow-bones. If it's damp in your hand it's no use to me and I'd rather you left it where it was.
quests.accept_text: Off the risen husks, wherever the field is thickest.
quests.turn_in_text:
Dry and pale. Every one.

I could carve a chapel out of these.

I'll settle for a comb. There's less call for chapels.

quests.title: Stings for the Apothecary
quests.description:
Wrenn. Reagents. Quickly, before Darne comes over and makes it a negotiation.

The windfall wasps in Malden's Orchard are full of a venom I have been trying to buy for years.

Years. I have written to the orchard. I have gone in person, twice, and stood at the gate like a fool.

The orchard won't sell it.

And I'd understand that if they were using it - they're not. Nobody at Malden's has any interest in the wasps at all. They simply will not have anyone in among the trees, and they have never once given me a reason.

The wasps won't sell it either, which is the only part of this arrangement I can respect.

So I'd like it taken.

North of the Raven Hill road.

The stings are on the abdomen. Handle them with tongs - mine, if you've none, and bring them back.
quests.accept_text: Malden's Orchard, north of the Raven Hill road. Use tongs.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six stings and no stinging.

You have steadier hands than most, and most of the people I send have been dead long enough to stop shaking.

quests.title: Names on the Stones
quests.description:
Reader Cass. Keep your voice ordinary - I've found it carries better than whispering out here.

I read the stones in the Raven Hill wing. That's my whole office and nobody assigned it to me.

Most of them are blank.

Rain does that, over long enough. I'd accepted rain for the first year.

Then I noticed the smooth ones aren't the oldest. They're scattered - a blank stone between two legible ones cut the same season by the same mason - and rain does not choose.

Something out there rubs back.

So I'd like three clusters visited and the weeds pulled away from them, while there's still something under the weeds.

West of the middle terrace.

And read them aloud when you find a name.

It helps. I can't tell you how I know that and I'm certain of it.

objectives.label: the upper stones of the Terrace
the stones by the Terrace path
the lower stones of the Terrace

quests.accept_text: Three clusters of stones in the graveyard wing, west of the middle terrace.
quests.turn_in_text:
Three more names.

I'll write them on the wall, so they stay. The wall's the only thing out here that hasn't been rubbed at.

quests.title: Sleepers That Won't
quests.description:
I count the sleepers each dusk.

Tomb-keeper. That's the post and the counting is the whole of it - I go along the chapel yard at the same hour and I count, and the number has been the same number for a long time.

Some of them have stopped lying down.

And I want to be precise about what's bothering me, because it isn't that they're up. Things get up in this valley. I've been doing this long enough.

It's where they go.

They wander off the Raven Hill plots looking for a bed. Not wandering generally - looking, going from plot to plot, and settling in one, and being moved on by whatever's already in it.

They're trying to lie down somewhere. They just can't find the right one.

So send them back where they belong.

Groundskeepers and husks both, south of the Keep.
quests.accept_text: At Raven Hill, south of the Keep.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fewer wanderers.

I'll sleep better.

Metaphorically. The joke's worn thin but it's the only one this post has got.

quests.title: Crows at the Gate
quests.description:
Crypt Guard Molsen. Don't laugh at this one. Everybody laughs at this one.

I am tired of the crows.

They pick at the Keep's banners - which is a supply problem, because a banner's a month's work and we've replaced three.

They steal buttons off my coat. I have four buttons. I had nine.

And one of them has learned to open the gate-latch.

That's where it stops being funny and I'd like a moment on it. Not knock it loose. OPEN it - from the top, with the beak, in the correct direction, which took it some working out and which it now does reliably.

A bird has solved the gate of a keep and nobody above me will put that in a report.

The Dead Field, east of the road.

The harrowers feed them. That's not a guess - I've watched it, and it's why the crows are here and why they're clever.

Thin both.
quests.accept_text: The Dead Field, east of the road. The harrowers and the crows they feed.
quests.turn_in_text:
The latch-crow? Dead.

Good. I'd started talking to it, which is the point a man should stop and ask for help.

I owe you a drink I can't taste.

quests.title: The Hermit's Oil
quests.description:
[The hermit does not come out of the lean-to. He has not come out of it since the Plague.]

My lamp is nearly dry.

That's the request. I'd make it shorter if I could.

Spider-fat burns clean. No smoke worth the name, no smell, and it lasts - I've burned every other thing a person can burn in here and I came round to spider years ago.

I cannot hunt it myself.

Not won't. Cannot. Spiders have opinions about hermits, and they have had three years to form them, and I have not got further than the trees since before the Keep had a garrison.

The Skittering Dark. Silverpine spiders. Clean glands - a torn one leaks all the way home and arrives as nothing.

And tell no one I asked.

Not the Commander. Not the Reader. Nobody at that keep knows I'm still here and I have put a great deal of effort into that.
quests.accept_text: Silverpine spiders in the Skittering Dark. Clean glands.
quests.turn_in_text:
I can read again.

Not that there is much I wish to read.

But there is a difference between choosing not to and not being able to, and I have missed the first one.

quests.title: The Pilgrim's Road
quests.description:
Osk. Pilgrim - that's what they put on the roster and I've never corrected it.

I walk between this Keep and Tirisfal every autumn.

To pray. That's what I say, and it's what I've said for eleven years, and everyone accepts it because nobody asks a pilgrim a follow-up question.

I have no idea who I'm praying to.

I want that said once, to somebody, before I go again - I knew, at the start. I'm sure of that much. And somewhere in the eleven years the walking stayed and the rest of it went, and I kept walking because the walking was the part I could still do.

So I'd like the road made less murderous.

That's all. It doesn't need to be safe - it's never been safe.

The woods north and east. Spiders, mainly, and the treants that have gone wrong.

I'll walk it once more before the snow either way.
quests.accept_text: The woods north and east of the Keep.
quests.turn_in_text:
A quieter road.

I'll walk it once more before the snow.

And I'll think about your question, which you were polite enough not to ask.

quests.title: A Cracked Locket
quests.description:
[Taken from inside a skeletal groundskeeper's rib-cage. Not a pocket - inside the ribs, where something would have had to put it deliberately.]

A cracked silver locket.

The crack runs across the face rather than the hinge, which means it was dropped or struck and not forced open.

There's a single pressed flower inside. Flat, colourless now, and whole - whoever closed this closed it carefully, and the flower has not shifted in however long it has been in there.

The silver is worn smooth at one edge. The way a thing goes when it's been held in the same hand, the same way, for years.

[There's a figure at the Keep who wanders the lower court. Answers to nothing in particular. Nobody at the Sepulcher has ever managed a name, and the Commander has stopped trying to put one on the roster.]

[It's worth showing to that one.]

objectives.label: Bring the locket to Something That Was Once Named in the lower court

quests.accept_text: The lower court of the Sepulcher - the one who answers to nothing in particular.
quests.turn_in_text:
...yes.

That one.

Thank you.

I think... I think I had a daughter.

quests.title: Wreaths for the Quiet
quests.description:
The Mourner. You can call me that, it's what everyone calls me and I stopped minding.

I weave wreaths out of what the dead leave behind.

Not for ceremony. There isn't a ceremony here anymore and there hasn't been since the Plague, and I'd not pretend otherwise to somebody standing in the yard looking at it.

The risen farmhands at Olsen's Farthing carry wilted sprays in their pockets.

Last year's offerings. Picked, bound, put in a coat - and never delivered, because the delivering is the part that stopped.

They're still carrying them. All of them. A field full of people walking about with flowers in their pockets for graves they were going to visit.

So I'd like them brought in.

South of the Keep, at the Farthing.

Wilted is fine. Wilted is what I work with and I've never once had anything else.
quests.accept_text: The farmhands of Olsen's Farthing, south of the Keep.
quests.turn_in_text: Even wilted, they mean something. I'll lay them where they were meant to go.
